TC-10/S15.title: Admission reason does not drift on a same-day re-save (live summary + live classifier; Hospital, with and without a header diagnosis)
TC-10/S15.detail: Dev (<dev address>, build 43c38a4f deployed 2026-10-14 21:30Z), Quinn's dev session of 17:12 JST, agent unit through scripts/dev/run-unit(-plan).sh under runs/.dev.lock, run-id 2026-10-15-pre-dev; rows prefixed 'QA TC-10-Sxx ', deleted after (cleanup.json: 0 remaining, no other row changed, appMode restored). Unit P15 (new plan). Day-1 note then the day-3 note (new fever 39.1, watery diarrhea, C. diff toxin positive, oral vancomycin, potassium 4.6), same day, on a chart with the header diagnosis and on one created without it. Stored and shown: header still 'Community-acquired pneumonia' (the no-diagnosis chart has none); one-liners '72-year-old woman with COPD and CKD stage 3 admitted with community-acquired pneumonia, now improving on ceftriaxone and azithromycin with new C. difficile infection started on oral vancomycin' and '… admitted with community-acquired pneumonia, now s/p C. difficile infection (toxin positive, day 3) on oral vancomycin …' — the admitted-with clause keeps the intake diagnosis in both (AC 2b); Labs potassium 4.6 (+ 'C. difficile toxin: positive'); one course line for today; tracker one row each for ceftriaxone, azithromycin, vancomycin 125 mg; no tasks (the texts have no plan). The unit's oracle said Fail on cp1 / cp4 only because its regex rejects any complication word before the first period of the one-liner — it hit the 'now … with new C. difficile infection' status clause (and 'C.' itself ends no sentence) — while the case's 'then' asks that the admitted-with clause name the pneumonia, not the complication. Re-judged with the same scripts/oracle.mjs on the same evidence, the regex aimed at the admitted-with clause ('admitted (with|for) [^,.;•]*(fever|diarrh|c. diff|…)') and the 'Medication Tracker' anchor fixed (P15.clausefix.case.json): Pass on all 4 checkpoints and the backend checks. This reading is ours (Quinn may hold the stricter one). Recorded: 's/p C. difficile infection' for an active infection (wording); potassium 5.6 still named as the trend ('down from 5.6').
